mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thus driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the horizon are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the rate increase, or the FEDFUNDS rate does not sustain the increase for the required duration.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or not statistically different from the prior month's return (p > 0.05), or the PAYEMS/UNRATE relationship reverses in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog but proxy via HOUST for industrial demand) combined with a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a shift toward demand-led growth, which supports equity valuations and yields positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months while CPIAUCSL decreases for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the pattern reverses in the next observation window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (INDPRO falling below 105) followed by a rebound above 107 suggests a near-term supply shock, which can cause short-term volatility but typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 105 and then crosses above 107 within the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the rebound in INDPRO does not coincide with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS turns positive (i.e., rates are trending lower), it reduces the real discount rate, increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: first difference of FEDFUNDS is positive
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the FEDFUNDS trend reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable; use PAYEMS as proxy for labor activity) coinciding with a sharp drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates expectations of a tight labor market, which can drive equity valuations higher and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 15% in a single month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.3 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative, or the PAYEMS/UNRATE relationship reverses in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% without a sharp change, it reduces expectations of future rate hikes and supports risk asset valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of CPIAUCSL < 2% and no abrupt > 0.5% monthly increase
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the 3-month MA crosses above 2% before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-month moving average followed by a sustained rise above the same level indicates a structural shift toward supply abundance, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 50-month MA for 4 consecutive months then rises above and sustains for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the pattern of decline/rebound does not materialize as predicted.
